top_news.title: When God plays Nigerian politics (1)
top_news.summary: Imagine a country where politicians gather in churches and mosques to seek divine intervention before elections, where candidates declare that God has chosen them to lead, where supporters describe electoral victories as miracles and where defeated candidates sometimes blame spiritual forces for their losses. Imagine further that, after these politicians assume office, citizens continue to struggle with poverty, insecurity, unemployment, corruption, injustice and the absence of basic necessities. One is then compelled to ask a fundamental philosophical question: if God participates in the politics of a nation, what kind of politics are human beings playing? Is God merely a spectator in the theatre of political ambition, or does divine wisdom, as understood in the various religious traditions of humanity, demand a different standard of leadership? The title “When God Plays Nigerian Politics” is not an attempt to glorify God, defend any religious institution or suggest that every political development in Nigeria is an act of divine intervention. articles.title: When God plays Nigerian politics (1)
articles.summary: Imagine a country where politicians gather in churches and mosques to seek divine intervention before elections, where candidates declare that God has chosen them to lead, where supporters describe electoral victories as miracles and where defeated candidates sometimes blame spiritual forces for their losses. Imagine further that, after these politicians assume office, citizens continue to struggle with poverty, insecurity, unemployment, corruption, injustice and the absence of basic necessities. One is then compelled to ask a fundamental philosophical question: if God participates in the politics of a nation, what kind of politics are human beings playing? Is God merely a spectator in the theatre of political ambition, or does divine wisdom, as understood in the various religious traditions of humanity, demand a different standard of leadership? The title “When God Plays Nigerian Politics” is not an attempt to glorify God, defend any religious institution or suggest that every political development in Nigeria is an act of divine intervention. Rather, it is an invitation to interrogate the relationship between divine authority, human ambition, political responsibility and the moral consequences of leadership.
